A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Glauber Generative Model work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original GGM language-generation perplexities and image-generation FIDs in Tables 1–2, alongside generated examples and nearest-neighbor analysis.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds a preliminary language-generation scaling result in Appendix K.

M1.justification: The noising process, binary-classification loss, reverse sampler, conditional inference and transformer design are retained. The explanation of computing vocabulary predictions in one forward pass and the larger experimental configuration do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Appendix K adds training on RedPajama for a preliminary language-generation scaling experiment. OpenWebText, CelebA-HQ, FFHQ and the existing infilling tasks remain; no additional application task is demonstrated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–2 is unchanged. MDLM already appears in v3 Table 1 and Appendix H.3; its expanded discussion in v4 does not introduce a baseline. Appendix K adds no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix K introduces an approximately 800M-parameter configuration evaluated using GPT2-xl, alongside the retained 387M-parameter experiment. Existing table protocols, metrics, sample counts and sampling settings remain unchanged. Remark 2 discusses published precision effects without documenting FP64 reruns of these comparisons.

E4.justification: Appendix K adds a preliminary check of improvement with increased model size and training data, reporting one additional configuration without separating the two factors. The existing iteration-count comparison, nearest-neighbor analysis and conditional-generation cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the experimental results. Existing averaging practices are unchanged, and the scaling result adds no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Appendix K newly reports GPT2-xl generative perplexity of 16.7 for the approximately 800M-parameter RedPajama model. The original 387M-parameter OpenWebText result remains 19.9 under that evaluator; these are different settings. Tables 1–2, figure results and generation examples otherwise retain their findings.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 and Appendix C add a finite-step output-distribution convergence theorem under perfect classification, extending the original forward-mixing and exact-reversal lemmas. Appendix A changes the coupling bound from T(1−epsilon)^(T/L) to L(1−epsilon)^floor(T/L), also stated in Lemma 1. However, new Equation 9 prints a negative exponent inconsistent with that decaying bound.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution section retain the same central reduction, performance and infilling claims. Section 5 modestly broadens its concluding statements about current performance limitations and future improvement from GGM specifically to discrete diffusion models generally.

C2.justification: Remark 2 adds an explanation, attributed to Zheng et al. (2024), connecting FP32 Gumbel-max truncation to effectively lower sampling temperatures in SEDD and MDLM. Appendix K interprets joint scaling as beneficial. v4 also removes v3's argument that planned non-release implies no tangible societal impact.

D1.justification: v4 removes the explicit statement that the authors do not intend to release the model publicly, without providing replacement access information. Detailed hyperparameters, hardware and baseline implementation references remain unchanged in v3 Appendix H and v4 Appendix I. This changes disclosure, without establishing changed availability.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds a focused discussion and references on Glauber/Gibbs mixing and applications, and expands MDLM's relationship to D3PM. Remark 2 adds Zheng et al. (2024) on categorical sampling. The central positioning against previous discrete diffusion approaches remains intact.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized explanatory edits, adds convergence and scaling subsections, removes the Societal Impact section, and updates affiliation, publication headers and citation style. Most prose and the overall narrative order are retained.

P2.justification: The ICLR template changes typography, table sizing and float placement. Figures 3–4 are grouped on page 10, and Figure 7 moves to a separate appendix page. Figures 1–8 retain the same artwork, and Tables 1–2 retain their comparison structure.

improvement.justification: The revised mixing bound and explicit initialization-error analysis modestly strengthen the theoretical account, while the sampling caveat and preliminary scaling result add useful context. Gains are limited by Equation 9's sign inconsistency, sparse documentation of the scaling experiment and removal of the model-release disclosure. The original empirical evidence remains intact.
